sermon.title: Gravel for the Grumbler
sermon.thesis: Right diagnosis, wrong prescription: Israel’s demand for a king like the nations rejects the Lord as King and plants a taking monarchy whose fruit Isaiah will later confront.

outline.body: Why is coveting the last commandment in Exodus 20? Ask the question. Leave the death spiral for the close.

outline.text: Samuel’s sons are part of the problem

outline.body: 1 Samuel 8:1–3 — Joel and Abijah take bribes and pervert justice. The gate is already broken.
Two defendants: the sons industrialize injustice; the people then covet a king like the nations.
Sinned-against people often sin in their response. Galatians 6:1: consider yourself, lest you also be tempted. 1 Corinthians 10:12: take heed lest you fall.
Wrong-form monarchy. Rehoboam is the terminus on October 18 (1 Kings 12; optional 14:25–28). Four generations of taking. Assyria waits for Isaiah 7.
2. The verb “take” (lqch) — eight takings; the sons first.
3. The unanswered cry (8:18) — leave it hanging.
Not anti-government. Isaiah’s defendants are those who industrialize taking (Isaiah 5:8; 3:14; 10:1). Takings began with the sons and became the ordinary economy.
Return to Exodus 20. Coveting drives the Isaiah death spiral: the sons take; the people, sinned against, then covet a king like the nations.
Communion: the spiral is taking. Jesus absorbs it with his own death. He does not take; He gives himself. Bread and wine they do not extract from a neighbor.
Optional: Matthew 27:18 / Mark 15:10 — delivered up out of envy.

Optional, once: Isaiah 11:1–5 — the shoot from Jesse, the King who judges the poor with righteousness (if Isaiah 11 speaks at the table, that is the Isaiah spend). Magnificat, Luke 1:52–53 — the hungry filled, the rich sent empty.

announcements.title: Men's Retreat
announcements.body: Men, mark your calendars for our annual Men's Retreat. Meet Justin Lackmacher, founder of Redemption House. Chris and Dov have gotten to know Justin over the years and are absolutely thrilled to have him spend time with the men at Providence. Justin is a former addict, a current minister to addicts, and — as Pastor Chris puts it — has serious Biblical Counseling game. Spots are limited; registration cost increases on October 12.
